description:
`jit doc add` refuses a text document whose content contains a demangled Rust symbol path, reading the symbol as a relative filesystem path and rejecting it as not lexically confined.

## Background

The asset scanner extracts path-like tokens from a document being linked so that referenced assets can be recorded. A committed profiler or disassembly dump contains symbols such as `memchr::arch::x86_64::memchr::count_raw::find_avx2`; the scanner treats the `::`-separated token as a relative path, fails confinement, and refuses the link for every document type. Committed perf attribution and assembly dumps therefore cannot be linked to the issue that produced them.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Linking a `.txt` document whose body contains `memchr::arch::x86_64::memchr::count_raw::find_avx2` succeeds for every document type, and the token is not recorded as an asset.
- [hard] REQ-02: A genuine relative path that escapes the repository in the same document is still refused with the existing confinement error.
- [hard] REQ-03: A regression test covers both cases.

## Notes

Observed in a downstream repository while linking `popcnt-attribution.txt`, a committed perf report.
title: Asset scanner reads demangled Rust symbols as paths
